doc: SCHEMA.md's filter micro-syntax, applied end to end: a query in, the ids it leaves out. Combination is one rule -- tokens AND, alternatives OR -- and both halves are pinned here: repeated keys narrow, `key:A|B' is the either. Browser-renderer only -- table-view.el's `/' is a plain substring over the row, with no grammar to hold to this. The `state:*...*' cases are a renderer's half of a producer meta: which keywords are in a group is the producer's to say, so the only term decidable here is the empty cell SCHEMA puts in `*active*'. The `*empty*' and multi-valued `*word*' metas need no producer at all, so both sides answer them alike and these cases bind both. Most cases share the file's `view'; a case may carry one of its own, either whole or as {"$ref": NAME} naming one of `views'.
